description: The hosted web app is the entire UI, so the IPC bridge must be exposed to its origin — that injection (window.__TAURI_INTERNALS__) is also how shell.ts knows it is inside this wrapper. Exposed: the opener scoped to https and mailto (Google OAuth in the system browser), and the shell's own show_banner command (title + body only, clamped in Rust) for PUSH/meeting banners. No notification-plugin command is granted: its notify accepts icon paths/attachments, and on Windows an icon becomes a file:/// image source. core:default is spelled out minus core:tray, core:menu, core:image and core:resources: the shell now compiles the tray feature, and core:default would otherwise let the page create, replace or hide tray icons and menus (and load images from a path). The remaining core sets are window/webview/app getters (plus Tauri's internal maximize and debug-only devtools toggles), path string helpers and events. No shell, fs, http, process or window-mutating permission: a compromised page could at worst open a browser tab or post a toast.
